acknowledgement.title: ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY
acknowledgement.sovereigntyStatement: The Woven Project and Common Threads extend our respects to all Indigenous Peoples who have travelled to be with us at this gathering. We look forward to hosting you in Gimuy.
paragraphs: We acknowledge and pay our respects to the Traditional Custodians of the land on which we will gather — the Gimuy Walubara Yidinji People — and neighbouring nations Yirrganydji, Djabugay, Buluwai, Madjandji, Dulabed and Malanbara Yidinji, Bundabarra and Wadjanbarra Yidinji, Mandingalbay Yidinji, Mamu and Ngadjon-Jii, and Gunggandji Peoples.

slides.heading: Where Collective Knowledge Leads To Collective Strength
paragraphs: Woven weaves global Indigenous knowledge and builds back our power for climate justice — strengthening the health of our planet while strengthening the rights of our people.

slides.heading: Beginning With The Rightful Return Of Lands
paragraphs: We envision a climate-stable future that includes, values, and upholds Indigenous peoples and Indigenous-led climate solutions, beginning with the rightful return of lands and territories.

slides.heading: A Vision Carried For Seventeen Years
paragraphs: Woven's roots trace to the Indigenous Peoples' Global Summit on Climate Change in Anchorage, Alaska, in 2009. Woven launched in 2025, and this is its first global gathering.

slides.heading: Land Back, Upholding UNDRIP, Data Sovereignty
paragraphs: We demand that Indigenous Peoples have full access and control over their lands and territories for climate action, of the development and use of their knowledges and data, and full recognition and implementation of UNDRIP for climate justice.

slides.heading: Dreaming Into Our Future
paragraphs: Woven’s inaugural gathering will convene fifty Indigenous leaders, knowledge holders, Elders and youth and climate champions from across the globe to gather in Australia, welcomed by local First Nations and invited into the cultural philosophy of Dreaming.
